claims.text: CrFeCoNiAl and CrFeCoNiSi alloys can form stable, coherent, slow-growing protective oxide layers above 900 °C.
Limited interdiffusion at the metal/oxide interface governs formation and persistence of the protective scale.
Selective segregation of Al or Si causes the limited interfacial interdiffusion.
Al promotes a coherent alumina scale, whereas Si promotes a coherent silica scale.
Alumina or silica acts as a barrier to further oxygen and metal-ion transport.
The comparison includes both single-phase and multiphase CrFeCoNiX solid-solution states with homogeneous elemental distributions.
CALPHAD can be used to calculate phase equilibria and high-temperature oxide formation as a function of oxygen partial pressure in CrCoFeMnNi.
DFT and CALPHAD modeling will be combined with targeted oxidation experiments at 950 °C.
Oxidation will be tested at 950 °C while systematically varying oxygen partial pressure.
Al or Si preferentially migrates to the metal/oxide interface at high temperature.
Interfacial Al or Si segregation reduces interdiffusion of oxygen and metal cations.
Reduced interdiffusion permits selective nucleation and parabolic growth of a coherent alumina or silica barrier.
Minimal ionic transport through the barrier prevents stress accumulation that would otherwise cause cracking or spallation.
The protective oxide is predicted to be continuous and adherent and to follow parabolic growth kinetics.
CrFeCoNiMn is predicted to be less effective than the corresponding Al- or Si-containing alloys at forming a protective diffusion barrier.
At 950 °C, absence of a Cr2O3 layer in CrMnFeCoNi was associated with continued outward Mn diffusion and Mn3O4 formation.
The proposed mechanism applies above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres and in both single-phase and multiphase states when oxide formation is diffusion controlled.
Rapid non-parabolic growth, frequent cracking or spallation, or diffusion measurements incompatible with barrier formation would falsify the proposed mechanism.
